messages:
Clara: quick q — Helix Health wants a short explanation for tenant provisioning on Private: who holds keys during onboarding, how we lock down RBAC changes during provisioning, and what audit logs we can produce. We have a review call tomorrow, any short summary?

Asha: short summary: we support two modes — customer-managed KMS (recommended) or Redwood-managed keys. For customer KMS we do envelope encryption: customer key encrypts DEKs, DEKs used by runtime. For on-prem Private we can accept HSM-imported keys. RBAC: provisioning uses a temporary "provisioner" role scoped to the provision job, auto-revoked after successful provisioning.

Ben: RBAC details: role templates = tenant-admin, tenant-operator, tenant-auditor. Provisioner is ephemeral service-account with TTL=15m by default; we can shorten to 5m for high-risk customers. We support OIDC-issued ephemeral certs and rotate service-account creds on every run.

Asha: Audit/logs we can stream: auth events, key unwrap/usage events, provisioning lifecycle events, policy changes. Example log schema (JSON):
```
{
  "ts": "2026-03-21T14:02:12Z",
  "actor": "svc:provisioner-helix-123",
  "action": "provision:tenant-create",
  "resource": "tenant/helix-123/config.yaml",
  "outcome": "success",
  "request_id": "req_0a1b2c3d",
  "kms_event": "DEK_wrapped_with_cmk",
  "trace_id": "trace-abc-123"
}
```
We can ship that as JSON over HTTPS to SIEM, or via syslog. Retention/format configurable per contract.

Diego: customer asked for a short proof we don't exfil keys during provisioning — can we give a step-by-step or an artifact they can sign off on?

Asha: yes — we have a "provisioning custody" artifact: ephemeral audit snapshot + signed manifest. Process: provisioner obtains ephemeral token -> creates tenant DEK locally -> DEK is wrapped by customer CMK (or Redwood KMS) -> wrapped DEK stored in tenant vault. We can export the audit snapshot and a signed manifest (deterministic hash of actions). Example CLI to produce snapshot: `redwoodctl prov snapshot --tenant helix-123 --request req_0a1b2c3d`

Ben: incident/IR Qs: if a runtime vuln is found affecting DEK handling, IR playbook: initial ack within 4 hours, containment in 24, full remediation & root cause in planned window (varies by severity). For enterprise we offer extended forensic retention (up to 13 months) and will provide filtered forensic exports (S3 signed URL or direct SIEM ingest). Standard retention is 90 days.

Clara: perfect. For the call can you include the short bullet list + the log schema and the sample CLI? Helix specifically wants to know we can shorten provisioner TTL and provide an audit snapshot on-demand.

Asha: will draft answers now and attach internal runbook link: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/provisioning-custody>. Also linking the HSM import guide for Private: <https://redwood.internal/docs/hsm-import>. @Diego can you join the call at 10:30 PT? :thumbsup:

Diego: yep, I'll be there.
